data.turoyo: U+bayto d̥kənna ebe, húlanle ṣoba. Hule ak+kallawatayḏa, bəṯr omar, ‘Ăḷa, lə+gbaʕna!’  ‘Qay lo+kəbʕatla?’

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (77/67)

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (92/54)

data.turoyo: faqat u isan, d yosəq ʕal qarʕe du ṭurano, mi səbba d kito ebe dayroṯe ġalabe w dkoṯe d ʕabode w qadiše w ṭuro ʕeloyo w hawa basəmto w atrawoṯe komaḥwe mine, ġalabe lu isan koḥolele, i naqqa d yosəq aʕle, w innu lə gbəʕ d noḥət mine ste w ġalabe koḥole hawxa lu ḥa d ḥozele.
data.translation: Aber wenn ein Mensch auf den Gipfel dieses Berges steigt, so wird er ihm doch wegen der vielen Klöster, die dort sind, und der Stätten der Gottesanbeter und heiligen, und weil der Berghoch ist und die Luft schön, und weil viele Orte von dort zu sehen sind, sehr gut gefallen, und er wird auch gar nicht wieder von ihm heruntersteigen wollen; und so gefällt er jedem, der ihn sieht. - Erzähler: Schabo aus Iwardo.

rationale: Unusual g-prefixed reduced gbəʕ under negation; source preserved, phonology left open.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (94/503)

data.turoyo: Bəṯr mu teʕmožo gbode hən b hən d motela l s i ḥawwe, yaʕni kobe d maḥwela, čoyakla bi hawwe.

summary: New idiom: hul d abəʕ lebe 'nach Herzenslust, bis zur Genüge (hier ironisch)'

data.headword: hul d abəʕ lebe 'nach Herzenslust, bis zur Genüge (hier ironisch)'
data.turoyo: Hanək ze mḥallale, hul d abəʕ lebe.
data.translation: Da verprügeln sie ihn wieder, solang sein Herz begehrte.

rationale: Unlisted heart-saturation formula with an ironic complete clause; phrase and bʕy 1 checked.

summary: Batch 1 reviews 150 explicit occurrences. Supplied count-only material: I Infectum sense 1 = 1023, Preterit Intransitive sense 1 = 82, Infectum sense 2 = 63, Infectum-wa sense 1 = 38. These are input counts, not independently computed corpus totals.

Personal wanting takes nominal, pronominal, relative or finite-clause stimuli. Clauses may have d- or no linker and may have a different subject. Necessity frequently uses a singular predicate with an l-series need bearer and a zero-marked required item; personal 'need' also occurs.
Requests with m-person and a desired clause remain sense 1: m- identifies the source of the desired action. Compare existing bʕy 1, 24/47. Speech-act force alone does not establish another sense.

Preterit Intransitive with a relative stimulus (JTM 4.1/9; 61/20) differs from an overt lexical nominal object. JTM 2.13/2 has nouns after abiʕi, but its choice construction is not an unqualified ordinary-volition counterexample.
47/7 has parallel d əbʕe clauses presenting hypothetical uses of money. The reader's asserted necessity is unproven; provisionally group with 1b rather than assert that building a house is required.

bʕy 1 was consulted in full. Want/need senses and Infectum shapes overlap this entry, including m-person plus clause. Preserve the supplied filing without claiming that every reduced form distinguishes the historical root. Searches for hul d abəʕ lebe and ibaʕu returned no hits.

61/163 is a provisional Preterit-wa witness contrasting with abiʕi in the same verse. JTM 3.2/11 əbʕiwo is an unresolved comparison, not independent confirmation; translation tense alone cannot settle the box.

Batch 2 checks 69 occurrences, bringing explicit occurrence coverage to 219 across both batches. This delta is cumulative: all earlier senses 1b–1d, examples, idiom and decisions in the previous batch remain in force.

62/79 independently confirms concessive 1d with kobəʕ plus ṭro-. The magical carpet requests do not justify further request senses: object/addressee suffixes and an omitted desired action or result location remain compatible with sense 1.

Reduced əbʕət / əbʕutu at 78/94 and 78/106 are provisionally Infectum, consistently with similar relative forms, not secure new Preterit Intransitive allomorphs. The earlier clear a-initial or abiʕ- witnesses remain distinct.

At 77/56 the input prints kobaʕle among repeated kobaʕla, whereas the existing example has -la throughout. Do not silently fix the entry from an uncollated variant. At 94/503 kobe lacks the final consonant; preserve the spelling without assigning it definitively to a historical root.

112/355 embeds a continuation marked 356 without a corresponding translation; 113/63 embeds 64; 101/28 is marked partial. No quotation from any of these rows was admitted. kobaʕni in 112/355 is not securely impersonal: ono and comparison with Kəbʕeni favor provisional personal sense 1.

Requests with m-person in 113/85 are merged into sense 1 under the batch-1 decision. The uncompleted request in Talay 1/139 supplies no Turoyo verb 'forgive'; the edition's parenthesized verb cannot establish another Turoyo sense.

Potential new research leads include l-suffix doubling/self-benefactive readings (103/15, 110/22), a required duration (115/267), and deliberative wanting/necessity (115/294). They do not warrant additional numbered senses here.
Confirm whether abiʕi rezo / abiʕi bərġəl (JTM 2.13/2) are ordinary 3pl Preterit Intransitive forms or a fixed choice formula.
Confirm ibaʕu (JTM 3.2/42) as Imperativ, its relation to bʕy 1 and whether 'good' is necessarily understood with l-beneficiaries.
Resolve Preterit-wa əbʕiwa (61/163) against Infectum-wa əbʕiwo (JTM 3.2/11); the reduced forms remain morphologically uncertain.
Check segmentation of gbaʕna (MAC Hanna Dewo/81), Kəbʕenən (PrS 41/120), Kəbʕeni (PrS 50/42), kəbʕalle (PrS 65/37) and əbʕalle (PrS 80/8).
Is hul d abəʕ lebe (41/36) a fixed saturation formula? The beating context is ironic.
Clarify kubʕət ba hno (JTM 3.3/13), the optional reading at 47/7 and dlobaʕ lébi (MAC Hanna Dewo/107).
Collate 77/56 kobaʕle against the entry's k-obaʕ-la; is the gender discrepancy a copying error, phonological change or referential shift?
Confirm kobən (77/67), gbəʕ (92/54), kobe (94/503), and əbʕiwayna (95/156), including the latter's possible Preterit-wa analysis.
Does -lux in 96/339 and 96/356 index a desired actor, addressee or object? Does 96/297 -lax address the vessel, and what is taṯi?
Supply the missing translation for the embedded continuation at 112/355 and resolve its verse number; also align the embedded 64 at 113/63 and the partial row 101/28.
Confirm kəbʕalli (110/22) as personal feminine plus self-benefactive versus an impersonal l-experiencer form; ono alone is not decisive.
Confirm the holder of -le in 115/267 and whether the deliberative kobəʕ in 115/294 is necessity or goal-directed wanting.
Verify the omitted desired predicate in Talay 1/139 from the source, without inventing a Turoyo 'forgive' form.
Capitalize the German noun 'Leiche'
rationale: German 'Leiche' is a noun and requires a capital L. The supplied translation of 96/311 also reads 'seine Leiche begraben'.

summary: Remove erroneous 'zu' after 'wollte'
rationale: The modal verb 'wollte' takes a bare infinitive, 'herausbringen'. The entry's intended translation of ubaʕ-wo d-mofaq-le is retained.

summary: The heart can stand for the human experiencer; this creates neither a separate 'like' sense nor proof of two zero-marked nominal arguments.
Cement, containers and animals extend the class of need bearers within the existing necessity sense.
Magical addresses extend the desired actor/theme to a vessel or carpet. A following location can describe the wanted result without creating a separate lexical sense.
Further heart-as-experiencer examples confirm the earlier participant extension.
